Reviewed the current published reference and its official OpenAPI specifications. Paths below are relative to `https://api.notion.com`; Admin paths include `/admin`. Deprecated legacy endpoints are listed separately.

**Cursor pagination — public API**

These endpoints accept `start_cursor` and return a continuation cursor. GET endpoints take pagination parameters in the query string; POST endpoints take them in the JSON body. Sources: [public OpenAPI specification](https://developers.notion.com/openapi.json), [pagination conventions](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro#pagination).

| Endpoint | Method | Path |
|---|---|---|
| List all users | GET | `/v1/users` |
| Retrieve block children | GET | `/v1/blocks/{block_id}/children` |
| Retrieve a page property item¹ | GET | `/v1/pages/{page_id}/properties/{property_id}` |
| List comments | GET | `/v1/comments` |
| List file uploads | GET | `/v1/file_uploads` |
| List custom emojis | GET | `/v1/custom_emojis` |
| List data source templates | GET | `/v1/data_sources/{data_source_id}/templates` |
| Query a data source | POST | `/v1/data_sources/{data_source_id}/query` |
| Search by title | POST | `/v1/search` |
| List views | GET | `/v1/views` |
| Get view query results | GET | `/v1/views/{view_id}/queries/{query_id}` |
| Query agents | POST | `/v1/agents/query` |
| List plugins | GET | `/v1/ai/plugins` |
| Query sessions | POST | `/v1/sessions/query` |
| Query session events | POST | `/v1/sessions/{session_id}/events/query` |

¹ Page-property pagination applies to list-valued properties, including `title`, `rich_text`, `relation`, and `people`; scalar properties return a single item. See [page property items](https://developers.notion.com/reference/property-item-object).

Two special cases:

| Endpoint | Method | Path | Pagination behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create a view query | POST | `/v1/views/{view_id}/queries` | Starts pagination: returns the first page and a `query_id`; continue using **Get view query results** above. |
| Append block children | PATCH | `/v1/blocks/{block_id}/children` | Describes its response as a paginated list, but accepts no continuation cursor. It is not an endpoint to repeatedly call for subsequent pages. |

Sources: [create a view query](https://developers.notion.com/reference/create-view-query), [append block children](https://developers.notion.com/reference/patch-block-children). Also, **Query meeting notes** (`POST /v1/blocks/meeting_notes/query`) explicitly does **not** support cursor pagination, despite returning `has_more`. See [meeting-note query behavior](https://developers.notion.com/reference/query-meeting-notes).

“Not specified” means the reference marks the item deprecated without identifying a `Notion-Version` that introduced the deprecation.

| Retrieve a database, legacy schema behavior | GET | `/v1/databases/{database_id}` | Schema retrieval → `GET /v1/data_sources/{data_source_id}`. The database endpoint remains available for the database container and its data-source list. | **2025-09-03** |
| Create a database, legacy request shape | POST | `/v1/databases` | Legacy combined database/schema operation → current Create database with `initial_data_source`; use `POST /v1/data_sources` for an additional data source. | **2025-09-03** |

| All operations returning page, block, database, or data-source objects | Various | Corresponding resource, list, query, and search paths | Response field `archived` → `in_trash` | Same timing: **April 2024**, removed in **2026-03-11**. |
| Operations reading or handling transcription blocks | Various | Block endpoints and other responses containing blocks | Block type/key `transcription` → `meeting_notes` | **2026-03-11** |
| Create template blocks | PATCH / POST | `/v1/blocks/{block_id}/children`; `/v1/pages` when supplying children | Creation of `template` blocks discontinued; no API replacement documented. | **March 27, 2023**; no version gate specified. |
| Update page markdown | PATCH | `/v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown` | `insert_content` → `update_content` or `replace_content` | **Not specified; documentation discrepancy noted below.** |
| Update page markdown | PATCH | `/v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown` | `replace_content_range` → `update_content` | **Not specified; documentation discrepancy noted below.** |
| List MCP client connections | GET | `/admin/v1/mcp_client_connections` | Query parameter `cursor` → `start_cursor` | **Not specified** |

Sources for legacy database operations and replacements: [legacy database reference](https://developers.notion.com/reference/post-database-query), [2025-09-03 upgrade guide](https://developers.notion.com/guides/get-started/upgrade-guide-2025-09-03). The List databases page carries a generic 2025 deprecation banner, but its text and the upgrade guide establish the earlier **2022-02-22 removal**.

Sources for renamed fields and block types: [2026-03-11 upgrade guide](https://developers.notion.com/guides/get-started/upgrade-guide-2026-03-11), [template-block deprecation](https://developers.notion.com/reference/block#template).

The markdown operation schemas explicitly contain `deprecated: true`, while the prose says the commands remain supported and “may be deprecated in a future version.” Treat them as legacy and migrate to the recommended replacements; the docs provide no reliable version date. See [markdown update reference](https://developers.notion.com/reference/update-page-markdown). Admin parameter deprecations appear in the [Admin OpenAPI specification](https://developers.notion.com/openapi-adminApi.json).

The deprecated database **filter**, **sort**, and **update property schema** reference pages describe parts of these legacy operations, rather than additional HTTP endpoints. Their replacements are the equivalent data-source filters, sorts, and property schemas in **2025-09-03**.

| Airline | Average departure delay¹ (minutes) | Departures delayed **more than 15 minutes** | BTS standard: **15 minutes or more** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| United (UA) | 12.74 | 20.50% | 21.33% |
| Alaska (AS) | 10.62 | 21.47% | 22.06% |
| Delta (DL) | 14.00 | 23.61% | 24.26% |
| Southwest (WN) | 21.87 | 37.86% | 39.71% |

**Exact source:** BTS TranStats, *Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance (1987–present)*, [July 2025 ZIP download](https://transtats.bts.gov/PREZIP/On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_1987_present_2025_7.zip), containing `On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_(1987_present)_2025_7.csv`. These are my aggregations of official records, rather than a published summary table.

**Calculation:** Filter `Year=2025`, `Month=7`, `Origin=SFO`, and `Reporting_Airline=UA/AS/DL/WN`. Use records with nonmissing `DepDelay`: United **5,059**, Alaska **1,020**, Delta **1,224**, Southwest **700**. Average = mean of `DepDelay`; requested percentage = count with `DepDelay > 15` divided by that same denominator. This includes records with a reported gate departure that were subsequently cancelled.

¹ `DepDelay` retains negative values for early departures. If you instead want early departures counted as zero, average `DepDelayMinutes`: United **15.67**, Alaska **13.73**, Delta **17.15**, Southwest **22.80** minutes. BTS defines `DepDel15` as **15 minutes or more**, which is why I’ve shown that separately from your strict “more than 15” wording. See the [official BTS field definitions](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/Fields.asp?gnoyr_VQ=FGJ).

Scope: reported domestic flights operated by these carriers; regional affiliates reporting under other carrier codes are excluded.

For **July 2025 domestic departures from SFO**, calculated from official DOT/BTS flight records:

| Airline | Average departure delay¹ | Departures delayed **more than 15 min** |
|---|---:|---:|
| United (UA) | 12.67 min | 20.45% |
| Alaska (AS) | 10.60 min | 21.39% |
| Delta (DL) | 14.00 min | 23.61% |
| Southwest (WN) | 21.84 min | 37.77% |

**Exact source:** BTS TranStats, *Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance (1987–present)*, [July 2025 official ZIP download](https://transtats.bts.gov/PREZIP/On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_1987_present_2025_7.zip), file `On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_(1987_present)_2025_7.csv`.

I filtered to `Origin = SFO`, July 1–31, 2025, and reporting carriers `UA`, `AS`, `DL`, `WN`. Canceled flights were excluded; diverted flights with recorded departures were included. These are the named operating/reporting airlines, excluding regional affiliates reporting separately.

¹ Average = mean of `DepDelay`, **including negative values for early departures**. The percentage = flights with `DepDelay > 15` divided by noncanceled departures with a recorded delay: United **1,034/5,056**, Alaska **218/1,019**, Delta **289/1,224**, Southwest **264/699**. See the [official BTS field definitions](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/Fields.asp?gnoyr_VQ=FGJ).

**Cutoff note for your slide:** BTS’s standard `DepDel15` measure means **15 minutes or more**, rather than strictly more than 15. Using that standard, the shares are **21.28%, 21.98%, 24.26%, and 39.63%**, respectively.
